Text_Reference: Abstract: 'We developed an alkaline solution (AKS) containing a combination of 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE), DMSO, D-sorbitol, and Tris for tissue clearing...'

Background: 'To reduce the difficulty and fluorescence quenching and improve the efficiency of tissue clearing, we reported a one-step method for tissue clearing based on an alkaline solution (termed AKS)...'

Results: 'To test the effects of different components of AKS on tissue transparency, we examined the effects of different components and their combinations on 300-μm-thick mouse brain slices... We termed this combination of reagents as AKS.'

General_Description.Text: AKS is an alkaline tissue-clearing reagent composed of Tris base, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE), and D-sorbitol. This method facilitates rapid clearing of both thin and semi-thick tissue samples while preserving and even enhancing the fluorescence of GFP and its variants. AKS is compatible with various fluorescent dyes and proteins, making it suitable for high-resolution 3D imaging and analysis of both mouse and human brain tissues, as well as other peripheral organs. The method is simple, requires only a single step, and is effective for time-sensitive experiments.
Text_Reference: Abstract: 'We developed an alkaline solution (AKS) containing a combination of 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE), DMSO, D-sorbitol, and Tris for tissue clearing... tested its clearing effect on samples from mice and human brains... AKS treatment rapidly cleared 300-μm-thick brain slices and 1-mm-thick slices from different organs within 5 min and 1 h, respectively. Moreover, AKS was compatible with a variety of fluorescence proteins and dyes. Most importantly, AKS enhanced the fluorescence of YFP...'

Results: 'AKS is an alkaline aqueous solution consisting of Tris base, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE), and D-sorbitol... The combination of 0.5 M Tris, 20% DMSO, 20% D-sorbitol, and 40% TDE (RI = 1.47) had the best clearing effect, with 300-μm-thick slices becoming transparent within 5 min...'

Discussion: 'To solve the problems of long processing time, complicated steps, and fluorescence quenching, all of which limit the application of tissue-clearing technology, here, we designed an alkaline tissue-clearing reagent AKS, a water-based ultrafast optical clearing method, containing Tris, D-sorbitol, DMSO, and TDE.'

Discussion: 'AKS is a simple and effective protocol for 3D imaging of various types of fluorescently labelled biological tissues... AKS has the advantages of ultrafast and simple tissue-clearing ability with wide compatibility...'

Time_Consumption.Text7: For clearing 0.1–1-mm-thick tissue sections, the slices were incubated with AKS. Typically, the clearing time was 5 min for the 300-μm-thick slices and 60 min for the 1-mm-thick slices. For clearing of hemibrains, the samples were incubated in AKS; typically, the hemibrains became transparent within 8h.
Text7_Reference: Methods section,'Tissue clearing with AKS':'For clearing 0.1–1-mm-thick tissue sections, after washing or labelling, the slices were incubated with AKS at room temperature with shaking at 80 rpm. Typically, the clearing time was 5 min for the 300-μm-thick slices and 60 min for the 1-mm-thick slices. For clearing of hemibrains, the samples were incubated in AKS at room temperature with shaking at 80 rpm in a 50-mL glass centrifuge tube with 30 mL of reagent; typically, the hemibrains became transparent within 8 h. Imaging was recommended to be performed immediately after tissue clearing.'

Tissue_Deformation.Text4: The morphological changes of 150-μm-thick sections from fresh-frozen Alzheimer’s disease (AD) samples after AKS treatment were relatively small.
Text4_Reference: Results section,'AKS enables 3D histopathology imaging of tissues from the human brain':'Since the preservation of tissue morphology and antigens is very important in pathological examination, 150-μm-thick sections from fresh-frozen Alzheimer’s disease (AD) samples were used for testing. First, we stained the samples with GFAP to label astrocytes, and then imaged the samples before and after clearing. We found that the morphological changes after AKS treatment were relatively small, and the images could be basically completely overlapped (Fig. 7B).'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text1: AKS was compatible with a variety of fluorescence proteins and dyes. Most importantly, AKS enhanced the fluorescence of YFP, in contrast to the majority of existing tissue-clearing methods which reduce the fluorescence intensity of fluorescent proteins.
Text1_Reference: Abstract: 'Moreover, AKS was compatible with a variety of fluorescence proteins and dyes. Most importantly, AKS enhanced the fluorescence of YFP...'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text2: The fluorescence of tdTomato, ChR2-EYFP, and YFP cleared by CUBIC-1, ScaleSQ (5), and AKS was well preserved, while the FOCM treatment reduced the fluorescence of tdTomato, ChR2-EYFP, and YFP. Moreover, the fluorescence of tdTomato, ChR2-EYFP, and YFP after the AKS treatment was stronger than that after the other three methods, and even stronger than that before clearing.
Text2_Reference: Results section, 'Wide compatibility with fluorescent proteins and fluorescent dyes': 'The fluorescence of tdTomato, ChR2-EYFP, and YFP cleared by CUBIC-1, ScaleSQ (5), and AKS was well preserved...'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text3: We found that under the conditions of imaging 10 min after clearing with AKS, most of the fluorescent signals were well preserved and only the fluorescence of Dylight405 was weakened. Also, even after 2 weeks of storage in AKS solution, most of the fluorescent signals were well preserved, indicating that tissue cleared with AKS was very stable.
Text3_Reference: Results section, 'Wide compatibility with fluorescent proteins and fluorescent dyes': 'We found that under the conditions of imaging 10 min after clearing with AKS, most of the fluorescent signals were well preserved...'

Preservation_Stability.Text1: To test the stability of the AKS-cleared tissue over time, we examined the effect of long-term processing of AKS on a variety of fluorescent proteins and fluorescent dye-labelled samples. We found that under the conditions of imaging 10 min after clearing with AKS, most of the fluorescent signals were well preserved and only the fluorescence of Dylight405 was weakened. Also, even after 2 weeks of storage in AKS solution, most of the fluorescent signals were well preserved, indicating that tissue cleared with AKS was very stable.
